veterans_affairs_ministers.name: Julian Fantino
veterans_affairs_ministers.notable: Minister during the 2014 closure of nine VAC regional offices, sparking the Equitas Society lawsuit and the 'Sacred Obligation' campaign. Shuffled out of portfolio January 2015 amid sustained criticism from veterans' advocates over service reductions.

veterans_affairs_ministers.name: Kent Hehr
veterans_affairs_ministers.notable: Inaugural Trudeau-era VAC Minister. Faced sustained criticism from veterans over the 2017 Pension for Life announcement which advocates argued reduced total lifetime compensation versus the pre-2006 Pension Act. Resigned from cabinet January 2018 over unrelated workplace-conduct allegations.

veterans_affairs_ministers.name: Seamus O'Regan
veterans_affairs_ministers.notable: Minister during Pension for Life rollout (April 2019). Presided over continued VAC backlog growth - disability benefit claims backlog exceeded 40,000 files by end of tenure.

veterans_affairs_ministers.name: Lawrence MacAulay
veterans_affairs_ministers.notable: Four-year VAC tenure spanning the 2022 disclosure that at least four veterans had been offered MAID by a single VAC service agent. Publicly pledged investigation; internal VAC review identified the agent and additional documented cases. Cross-axis: also in Indigenous file as Indigenous Services 2023.

veterans_affairs_ministers.name: Ginette Petitpas Taylor
veterans_affairs_ministers.notable: VAC 2023-2025 under continued fallout from VAC-MAID disclosures. Oversaw the PPCLI class-action (mould / contaminated housing at CFB Shilo and CFB Petawawa) - lawsuits filed against DND/CAF for substandard base housing.

veterans_affairs_ministers.name: Emmanuella Lambropoulos
veterans_affairs_ministers.notable: Current Minister under Carney government. Holds the portfolio during continued litigation, backlog reduction commitments, and CAF recruitment/retention crisis affecting future veteran population.

deputy_ministers_vac.name: Walter Natynczyk
deputy_ministers_vac.notable: Former Chief of the Defence Staff (2008-2012). Served as VAC Deputy Minister for eight years - spanning Fantino closures, Hehr Pension for Life rollout, O'Regan/MacAulay handover, and the 2022 VAC-MAID disclosure. Longest-serving DM of the modern VAC. Departed 2022.

deputy_ministers_vac.name: Paul Ledwell
deputy_ministers_vac.notable: DM during the public disclosure of the VAC-MAID cases (November 2022). Senior departmental lead on investigation response and on the retraining / protocols announced in 2022-2023.

veterans_ombuds.name: Guy Parent
veterans_ombuds.notable: Second Veterans Ombudsman. Eight-year tenure spanning the VAC regional-office closures and the Equitas litigation. Published multiple systemic reports on benefits-administration delays and adjudication inconsistency.

veterans_ombuds.name: Craig Dalton
veterans_ombuds.notable: Third Veterans Ombudsman. Issued the 2020 and 2022 annual reports documenting the disability-benefit backlog (peaked >23,000 files over service standard) and the VAC-MAID disclosure. Departed 2023.

veterans_ombuds.name: Nishika Jardine
veterans_ombuds.notable: Fourth Veterans Ombud, first woman. Responsible for post-MAID-disclosure systemic oversight, PPCLI housing-litigation watch, and recruitment-retention crisis monitoring.

vac_maid_documented_witnesses.name: Christine Gauthier
vac_maid_documented_witnesses.notable: Retired CAF corporal, Paralympian. Testified to the ACVA House of Commons committee December 1 2022 that a VAC service agent had offered her MAID when she sought a wheelchair ramp. Testimony corroborated by internal VAC documents and became the central case of the VAC-MAID disclosure.

vac_maid_documented_witnesses.name: Bruce Moncur
vac_maid_documented_witnesses.notable: Afghanistan war veteran (Operation MEDUSA, 2006), head-injury survivor. Publicly documented being offered MAID by a VAC service agent. Among the first veterans to speak openly about the disclosure, feeding the media and committee record that forced Minister MacAulay's investigation.

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Stephen Harper
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: PM during the 2006 New Veterans Charter (lump-sum replacement of lifetime pension). Closed nine VAC regional offices 2014. Faced sustained 'Sacred Obligation' campaign. Tenure coincided with rising CAF veteran suicide reporting in the DND/CAF Suicide Reports series.

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Justin Trudeau
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: Nine-year PM. Tabled Pension for Life (2017, in force 2019). PM during VAC-MAID disclosure (November 2022), PPCLI housing litigation, and the recruitment-retention crisis (CAF short ~16,500 regular-force positions by 2024). Pledged reversal of Harper-era service cuts; backlog persisted.

prime_ministers_of_record.name: Mark Carney
prime_ministers_of_record.notable: Current PM. Holds responsibility for continued VAC-MAID investigation follow-through, PPCLI housing litigation response, and the CAF recruitment commitment. Cross-axis: in Carney-Brookfield and Indigenous dossiers.

timeline.event: New Veterans Charter in force. Lifetime pension (Pension Act 1919) replaced for new claimants with lump-sum disability award + earnings-loss benefit.
Equitas Society files litigation alleging federal government breach of Sacred Obligation doctrine.
Closure of nine VAC regional offices announced by Minister Fantino.
Walter Natynczyk sworn in as Deputy Minister of VAC.
Trudeau government takes office, commits to reopening VAC regional offices and restoring lifetime pension option.
Pension for Life enters force. Disability-benefit backlog begins sustained growth.
Veterans Ombudsman 2019-2020 Annual Report documents backlog over service standard exceeds 23,000 files.
Initial media reporting that a VAC service agent had offered MAID to a veteran seeking disability support.
Christine Gauthier testifies to ACVA that a VAC service agent offered her MAID when she sought a wheelchair ramp.
VAC Minister MacAulay confirms to House of Commons that at least four cases identified, same service agent implicated.
VAC releases internal review; service agent no longer with department. Retraining protocol announced.
PPCLI class action filed re: mould and contaminated housing at CFB Shilo / CFB Petawawa.
DND/CAF confirms shortfall of approximately 16,500 regular force positions. Recruitment-retention crisis framed by CDS as existential.
Carney government takes office. VAC-MAID investigation follow-through and PPCLI litigation inherited.

statutory_framework: Department of Veterans Affairs Act - R.S.C. 1985, c. V-1
Canadian Forces Members and Veterans Re-establishment and Compensation Act (New Veterans Charter) - S.C. 2005, c. 21
Veterans Well-being Act (Pension for Life amendments) - S.C. 2018, c. 12
Criminal Code - ss. 241 and 241.2 (MAID eligibility and safeguards)
commissions_and_inquiries: House of Commons Standing Committee on Veterans Affairs (ACVA) - VAC-MAID hearings 2022-2023
Equitas Society v. Canada (ongoing federal litigation)
DND/CAF Report on Suicide Mortality in the CAF (annual series)
implementation_tracking: VAC Disability Benefits Backlog - service standard tracker
ACVA committee reports with government responses
accountability_chain.result_2025: VAC-MAID: at least four documented cases tied to one service agent; no criminal charges laid; internal retraining only. Disability-benefit backlog: down from 2020 peak but ~6,000 files remained over service standard at the end of 2024. PPCLI housing litigation: unresolved as of 2025. CAF recruitment shortfall: ~16,500 regular-force positions. CAF veteran suicide rate: elevated versus general population per the DND/CAF Suicide Reports series.
